messages:
Maya: Heads up — nightly perf shows a regression after the flash-alt fused-attn rollout. seq_len=2048 runs have ~15% lower throughput and higher tail latency, looks tied to KV-cache write contention.
Jorge: ugh, can you paste the nsys summary? rough percentages are fine.
Maya: pasted a trimmed nsys kernel table from the run: 
```
nsys summary: total GPU time 312ms
kernel: flash_alt_fwd_kernel        134.3ms   43.0%  (many launches)
kernel: kv_cache_write_sgd         82.6ms    26.5%  (serializing writes)
kernel: flash_alt_bwd_kernel       45.0ms    14.4%
kernel: memcopy_h2d                 20.1ms    6.4%
other kernels                     30.0ms    9.6%
```
Maya: The timeline shows kv_cache_write bursts overlapping with flash fwd launches which pushes SM occupancy lower and increases serialization.
Elena: can you share the exact repro command and the model/commit?
Maya: repro: 
```
nsys profile -o /tmp/tr -t cuda,nvtx python run_infer.py --model redwood/llama-70b --seq_len 2048 --batch 2 --kv-mode=shared --kernel=flash-alt
```
Maya: commit a3d9f7b (PR #2348) is the rollout that flipped fused behavior and the kernel-selection heuristic.
Sam: I ran a quick variant locally: disabling fused flash (force old flash) removes the write spike — KV write drops from ~82ms to ~18ms and throughput returns. So it's definitely interaction between fused variant and our KV write path.
Priya: noted. The kernel selector change in a3d9f7b added a fallback that attempts to pipeline KV writes into the same stream as attention to reduce memcpy. Could be exposing a serialization bug.
Jorge: any perfetto traces? timeline view helps see overlap across CUDA streams.
Maya: uploaded perfetto to the perf storage: perfetto://redwood/traces/1799001111/ (private link) — timeline shows KV write on stream 5 repeatedly waiting on mutex inside kv_manager.cu at ~t=120ms.
Sam: interesting — the mutex callsite is the path that writes cache entries when we evict prefixes. Maybe fused-attn increases frequency of small writes which amplifies the lock contention.
Elena: can we get nsight-systems with API trace to see NVTX markers around kv write? Also capture kernel launch parameters to check grid/block dims.
Maya: yes, I'll capture with NVTX markers enabled. command: 
```
nsys profile -o /tmp/trace -t cuda,nvtx --capture-range=nvtx python run_infer.py --seq_len 2048 --batch 2
```
Priya: quick mitigation idea: change heuristic to prefer smaller batch sizes for fused flash when seq_len > 1024, or route KV writes to a dedicated stream to decouple them from fused kernel launches. Might be a low-risk rollback until we root cause.
Jorge: agree. Also add a microbenchmark that exercises frequent small KV writes so CI fails fast.
Maya: FYI, perf-bot alerted: 
```
perf-bot: nightly/regression/eng-runtime failed on 1799001111 — throughput -15% vs baseline, alert P2. Linked traces: perfetto://redwood/traces/1799001111/, nsys /tmp/trace.qdrep
```
Sam: I'll try forcing KV writes to async stream and run nsys — quick experiment will show if decoupling helps.
Elena: if async stream helps, we should still add a proper fix in kv_manager (eliminate lock or coalesce writes).
Priya: let's schedule a short pairing session today 11:30 to reproduce and decide rollback vs mitigation. I've added a TODO card in the eng runtime board.
Jorge: ping @Maya when the NVTX-captured trace is ready, I'll grab grid/block params and check kernel compile flags (fused vs non-fused codepaths emit different PTX).
Maya: trace uploaded. Also attaching the tiny repro script in the channel gist: https://gist.redwood/run-kv-repro (contains toggles for kernel selection and kv-mode).
Sam: quick note — when I profiled with `cuda-memcheck` off, behavior differs (less stalling) which suggests async memory copies interplay. We should verify stream priorities too.
Priya: good call. We'll inspect stream priorities and whether fused kernel uses default stream which can cause implicit syncs.
Maya: thanks all — will follow up after 11:30 pairing with a short summary + proposed mitigation PR (likely route KV writes to stream 12 and add coalescing). :thumbsup:
perf-bot: reminder — add the new microbench to CI matrix so future rollouts catch this pattern early.
